{"subject":"p99 latency on your Cassandra leaderboard cluster","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. Your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard stuck with me, especially the work on tail latency and GC/compaction tuning.

That's the area ScyllaDB was built for: a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, so p99 latency stays predictable without the GC tuning cycle.

If it's useful, I'm happy to share how that design handles leaderboard-style workloads. Would that be worth a look?

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB
